stories.headline: D&B Introduces Agentic AI for Compliance and Third-Party Risk — Cutting Workflow Time from Days to Seconds
stories.summary: Dun & Bradstreet has announced agentic AI capabilities targeted at compliance and third-party risk workflows, promising to compress multi-day processes into seconds. This is a direct product move — not a roadmap item — deploying D&B's proprietary entity resolution and commercial data as the ground-truth layer powering autonomous risk agents. It validates D&B's 'AI Decision Intelligence' positioning in practice: the moat isn't the agent, it's the 600M+ record data foundation the agent runs on.

stories.headline: Moody's Launches MCP App Giving AI Agents Direct Access to Credit Ratings on 600M+ Companies
stories.summary: Moody's has launched a Model Context Protocol app that connects proprietary credit ratings and company data on more than 600 million public and private businesses directly into agentic AI workflows — highlighted by Anthropic as a key financial services data partner alongside Verisk. This is a significant competitive signal: Moody's is racing to become the embedded credit intelligence layer inside AI agents, precisely the 'neutral data layer' territory D&B is also targeting. The overlap with D&B's entity coverage and Paydex/commercial credit assets makes this a direct strategic collision worth watching.

stories.headline: Salesforce Agentforce Hits $800M ARR, Up 169% Year-over-Year — Proof Enterprise Agent Spend Is Now Committed Budget
stories.summary: Salesforce's Agentforce platform reached $800 million in annual recurring revenue in Q4 fiscal 2026, closing 29,000 deals and processing 2.4 billion agentic work units — shifting enterprise AI agents from pilot budgets to renewable, strategic spend. For D&B, this is critical market validation: Agentforce is one of the platforms D&B's 'be everywhere' strategy targets for embedding, and its rapid scale means the window for becoming the default B2B data layer inside Salesforce agents is narrowing fast. Anthropic's share of enterprise LLM spend also rose sharply from 24% to 40% year-over-year in the same period.

stories.headline: Gong Rolls Out September 2026 Agent Updates: Natural-Language Agent Builder and Enriched Account Data Integration
stories.summary: Gong's September 2026 product release includes a natural-language agent builder — where sellers describe what they want and Gong automatically configures the agent — plus the ability to pull trusted external account and contact data directly into Gong workflows. The data enrichment move is notable: it signals Gong is actively closing its long-standing gap on firmographic and account intelligence, which has historically been D&B and ZoomInfo territory. If Gong begins embedding third-party commercial data natively, D&B's Gong partnership and data licensing opportunity becomes more urgent to formalise.

stories.headline: U.S. Small Business Bankruptcy Filings Surge 63% Year-over-Year in August 2026 as Tariff and Cost Pressures Bite
stories.summary: August 2026 U.S. bankruptcy data shows Subchapter V Chapter 11 elections — the small business restructuring track — surged 63% year-over-year to 302 filings, with overall commercial filings also edging higher. The pressure is compounded by the U.S. imposing 50% tariffs on $27.6 billion of Canadian imports in August, followed by Canada's retaliatory 15–50% tariffs on 700+ U.S. products on September 8. For D&B, this is direct demand signal for Paydex monitoring, payment stress analytics, and supply chain risk products — the exact use cases where real-time commercial credit data has highest urgency for enterprise buyers.

stories.headline: Cognition AI Doubles to $48B Valuation in Four Months, Raising $2B Series E for Devin Coding Agent
stories.summary: AI coding startup Cognition raised $2 billion in a Series E led by Andreessen Horowitz and Accel on September 8, nearly doubling its valuation from $26B to $48B in just four months. Annualized run-rate revenue grew 83% from $492M to $900M since May, with enterprise clients including Mercedes-Benz, NASA, Goldman Sachs, and Citi. The raise signals investors see room for multiple large winners in agentic software engineering — a market framed not as developer tooling but as software labor at scale.

stories.headline: GPT-6 Astra Launches Alongside Claude Fable 5.1 and Gemini 3.8 Flash in Densest Frontier Release Wave of 2026
stories.summary: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta each shipped new frontier models within a 72-hour window in the first week of September, the most compressed multi-lab release cycle since August. OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra moved from limited preview to broad availability across ChatGPT, Azure, and AWS Bedrock on September 4; Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5.1 and a gated cybersecurity variant on September 1; Google released Gemini 3.8 Flash with a Fairwind-gated cyber tier on September 2. The defining pattern is a split between a model's raw intelligence and its permission layer — all four labs now ship general releases alongside restricted cyber-capability tiers, with access regimes diverging even as raw capabilities converge.

stories.headline: PwC Projects $31.6 Trillion in Global AI Infrastructure Spend Through 2050 — Power Identified as the Decisive Bottleneck
stories.summary: PwC's Global Data Centre Outlook, published September 2, forecasts $31.6 trillion in cumulative global AI infrastructure capital expenditure through 2050, with annual data centre capex rising from roughly $800 billion in 2026 to $1.8 trillion by mid-century. Chip upgrade cycles — not construction — will drive the majority of long-run spending, but power availability is identified as the decisive factor shaping where investment flows. Trade disruption to chip supply chains could cut global investment by nearly 20%, while a growing sovereignty push would redistribute rather than reduce it.

stories.headline: Trump Announces AI Czar and 'AI Force' While Newsom Issues Executive Order on AI Kill Switch — US Policy Fractures Along Federal-State Lines
stories.summary: President Trump posted plans on September 21 to create a new AI policy 'czar' and an 'AI Force' to promote and police artificial intelligence within existing laws, framed as an alternative to new federal legislation. The same week, California Governor Gavin Newsom issued an executive order seeking new state-level AI oversight mechanisms and floated a kill-switch provision for AI systems, explicitly positioning the move as a counterweight to Trump's deregulatory stance. The moves harden the federal-state fault line: Washington is betting on light-touch promotion while Sacramento is moving toward structured oversight, creating a compliance patchwork that AI vendors operating across jurisdictions will have to navigate simultaneously.

stories.headline: Frontier Overhangs: Why Model Leadership Is No Longer a Sustainable Business Moat
stories.summary: Ben Thompson argues the AI industry has accumulated five simultaneous overhangs — excess capability, excess products, excess pricing, excess capital, and excess safety positioning — and that absolute frontier model performance is no longer sufficient to build durable competitive advantage. The key structural shift: model and application layers are decoupling into modular architectures, with platforms like Microsoft Copilot now running GPT, Anthropic, and open-source models interchangeably through the same harness. Thompson invokes Clayton Christensen's modularity theory to explain why competition is migrating from raw capability to speed, convenience, and customisation. For D&B, this is the 'be everywhere' thesis validated in real time — as model choice commoditises, the proprietary data layer (DUNS, Paydex, entity resolution) becomes the durable differentiator that makes any harness decisively better, regardless of which model sits underneath.

stories.headline: Trusted Agentic AI Landscape Q3 2026: Lock-in Has Migrated from the Model Layer to the Stack Layer
stories.summary: Kai Waehner's Q3 2026 update to his enterprise agentic AI vendor landscape argues that the locus of vendor lock-in has fundamentally shifted — away from which frontier model an enterprise chooses and toward the broader stack layer: orchestration, data access, identity, and governance infrastructure. The analysis, covering Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, AWS, OpenAI, Salesforce, SAP, and others, positions trust and flexibility as the two decisive axes for every enterprise AI vendor decision in 2026. A US export-control episode that temporarily suspended access to frontier models accelerated enterprise awareness that model dependency is a fragility, not a strategy. This maps directly onto D&B's neutrality positioning — as a vendor-agnostic data and entity resolution layer that sits above model politics, D&B becomes more strategically valuable the more enterprises fear stack-level lock-in.

stories.headline: 2026 State of AI Agents: Governance and Evaluation Are Now the Primary Production Bottleneck
stories.summary: Databricks' 2026 State of AI Agents report, drawing on usage data from over 20,000 global customer organisations including more than 60% of the Fortune 500, finds that multi-agent system adoption grew 327% in under four months — but that the rate-limiting factor has moved firmly from deployment to governance and evaluation. Companies using evaluation tooling get nearly six times more AI projects into production; those using AI governance frameworks achieve over twelve times the production rate. More than 80% of databases are now being built by AI agents, creating urgent demand for a new category of database architecture designed for agent-native access patterns. For D&B, this is a strong structural signal: as agentic workflows scale, the need for a trusted, governed, entity-resolved data layer — one that agents can query with confidence — becomes a production requirement, not a nice-to-have.
stories.source: Databricks Research, databricks.com — 2026 State of AI Agents report

data_science.tagline: The shared memory layer that stops your ML teams from rebuilding the same features over and over — and keeps training and serving in sync.
data_science.what_it_is: A Feature Store is a centralized data system purpose-built for machine learning features. It sits between your raw data pipelines and your models, storing precomputed, versioned, and reusable feature vectors that any model — in training or live production — can consume. Think of it as a curated library of 'signals': instead of every data scientist writing their own version of 'days since last payment' or 'rolling 90-day revenue trend,' those calculations are computed once, registered, and shared. Two distinct stores usually coexist inside: an offline store (a columnar warehouse like Parquet/Delta Lake, optimized for batch training) and an online store (a low-latency key-value store like Redis or DynamoDB, optimized for real-time inference). The Feature Store ensures both stores serve the exact same feature logic — eliminating training-serving skew, one of the most insidious sources of silent model failure in production.
data_science.how_it_works:
1. FEATURE DEFINITION — Engineers write feature transformations in Python (or SQL) and register them with the store using a schema: name, entity key (e.g. DUNS number), data type, freshness SLA, and owner. Tools like Feast, Tecton, and Databricks Feature Store use a FeatureView abstraction for this.

2. MATERIALIZATION — A scheduler (Airflow, Spark, dbt) runs the transformation logic on raw source data and writes results into both the offline store (historical snapshots, keyed by entity + timestamp) and the online store (latest value, keyed by entity ID). Point-in-time correctness is critical: the offline store must support time-travel queries so training data reflects only what was knowable at that moment — no future leakage.

3. TRAINING RETRIEVAL — A data scientist calls get_historical_features(entity_df, feature_refs), passing a DataFrame of (entity, event_timestamp) pairs. The store performs a point-in-time join, returning the feature values that existed at each timestamp. This produces a training dataset that is reproducible and leak-free.

4. SERVING RETRIEVAL — At inference time, the application calls get_online_features(entity_ids, feature_refs). The online store returns the freshest materialized values in single-digit milliseconds. The model scores immediately without waiting for any computation.

5. GOVERNANCE & DISCOVERY — A feature registry UI lets teams search for existing features, see lineage (which pipelines produce them, which models consume them), monitor staleness, and flag deprecated features. This prevents the classic problem where three teams each independently compute 'company headcount growth rate' with slightly different logic.
data_science.when_to_use: Use a Feature Store when: (a) you have more than 2-3 models in production and notice teams duplicating feature logic; (b) you are experiencing training-serving skew — model performance in training looks great but degrades live; (c) you need sub-100ms feature retrieval at inference time for real-time scoring; (d) regulatory or audit requirements demand reproducible, point-in-time accurate training sets; (e) you are building agentic AI pipelines where multiple agents need to share the same live business signals. Avoid over-engineering a Feature Store for a single prototype model or pure batch-only use cases — a simple feature table in a data warehouse is sufficient there. The real ROI kicks in at organizational scale: many models, many teams, shared entities.
data_science.worked_example:
D&B's DUNS number is the perfect entity key for a Feature Store. Consider the six agent archetypes — Prospecting, Account Intelligence, Pipeline Risk, Territory Planning, Account Expansion, and Fleet & Asset. Each agent needs overlapping signals about a company: Paydex score trajectory, days-beyond-terms trend, employee count change, firmographic segment, subsidiary count, and technographic signals. Without a Feature Store, each agent's underlying model computes these independently — different freshness, different logic, guaranteed drift. With a Feature Store: 

• ENTITY KEY: D-U-N-S Number (resolves across all 600M+ records, handles entity hierarchy via corporate family trees). 

• REGISTERED FEATURES (examples): paydex_90d_avg (rolling 90-day Paydex mean, refreshed daily), dbt_trend_60d (days-beyond-terms slope over 60 days — a leading indicator of credit stress), employee_growth_yoy (year-over-year headcount % change), subsidiary_count (depth of corporate family tree), technographic_crm_flag (boolean: uses Salesforce/HubSpot). 

• OFFLINE USE: The Pipeline Risk & Revenue Protection agent's churn model calls get_historical_features() with a DataFrame of (DUNS, opportunity_close_date) pairs. It gets the exact Paydex and DBT values that existed at close — no leakage from subsequent payment events. Training is reproducible and auditable. 

• ONLINE USE: When a Prospecting agent evaluates a new lead in real time inside Microsoft Copilot or Salesforce Agentforce, it calls get_online_features(duns_id) and gets back all five features in <20ms — no live joins against the full D&B graph required. 

• EXPLAINABILITY PAYOFF: Because every feature has a registered definition and lineage, the Explainability First / Ground Truth principle is built in. A sales rep can ask 'why is this account flagged as high risk?' and the system can trace the answer to a specific, audited Paydex trend — not a black-box embedding. This is exactly the kind of structural moat that makes D&B's data layer defensible inside any agentic platform.
resources: Feast open-source Feature Store documentation and architecture guide (feast.dev) — the most widely deployed open-source option, good for understanding core concepts like FeatureView, materialization, and point-in-time joins

'Rethinking Feature Stores' by Tecton (tecton.ai/blog) — practitioner-level deep dive into training-serving skew, online/offline symmetry, and the operational challenges of production feature pipelines
'Machine Learning Engineering' by Andriy Burkov, Chapter 6 — concise, vendor-neutral treatment of feature pipelines, storage patterns, and the organizational case for a shared feature layer
